I used to install the accessories in cop cars and it's mostly junk. I can't believe how junky, heavy, and outdated the super expensive equipment was. Their cars were falling apart before they found me. They were wiring rat's nests and the factory designed mounting systems for the components failed constantly. Nothing like a siren stuck between the radiator and fan to cut your high speed pursuit short, or getting a black eye from a swinging dash cam!. I actually built my own wiring harnesses and stronger brackets and installed everything to the same level, or better, than a factory would. I did eight new cars for the department and charged on average, about $2500 per car in labor, to install $20k worth of equipment. It took me about a week to do each car. They decided to take them back to the guy that charged $400 per car. Then they'd bring them to me once a month for little issues and get a $300 bill to fix his terrible work. After 8 months, they ended up paying $2700 to finally get a reliable car. Government at work!

None of the cars I built ever had a problem once I was done with them.
